intent: The Games most people can name but cannot place in time: a marble stadium on a moving map, the 241-athlete counter against an erased 'women competed', then the first marathon drawn from Marathon into the stadium with a runner riding the line.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Where were the FIRST modern Olympics held?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Where were the first modern Olympics held?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Athens. On 6 April 1896 the first modern Games opened in a stadium rebuilt in marble.

lines.direction: hold on Attica; the athlete counter runs 0 → 241 on 'athletes' with the stadium tag; a flag sticker on 'nations'; the ANY WOMEN plate is struck through on 'women'; the French flag-ball thinks on 'Paris' and Greece pulses
lines.text: Just 241 athletes from 14 nations, all of them men. Women first competed in Paris, 4 years later.

lines.direction: dive to ×5 over the course; the Marathon pin and tag on 'marathon'; a runner rides the drawn line into the stadium until 'stadium'; the SPYRIDON LOUIS card and a water-drop sticker on 'carrier' as Greece pulses
lines.text: The marathon ran 40 kilometres from Marathon into the stadium. A Greek water carrier won it.

lines.direction: ease back over Greece; the CONNOLLY card on 'champion'; a jumping sticker on 'jump'; a graduation cap on 'Harvard' as the Greek flag-ball grins and Greece pulses; the Athens pin leaves at the end
lines.text: The first champion was an American, James Connolly, in the triple jump. He had left Harvard to come.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: Marble, flags, a water carrier. Follow us.
